canvas-01-1.description: This part of sheet 57, the title sheet of the Lavallette and Ortley section of the New Jersey coast volume, shows the bay side of southern Lavallette, drawn at 120 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from Washington Avenue at the top to Newark Avenue and the Lavallette borough line at the bottom, between the shore of Barnegat Bay on the west and Baltimore Avenue on the east. The Boulevard curves along the bay shore through the whole part, and the cross avenues, Washington, Brooklyn, New Brunswick, Virginia, Pennsylvania, New York, New Jersey, Jersey City, Princeton, Elizabeth and Newark, run from it east to Baltimore Avenue. The blocks between the Boulevard and Baltimore Avenue are divided into numbered lots of Sections C and D of the resort plan; those north of New York Avenue are cut short on the west by the curve of the Boulevard. No buildings are drawn: the whole part is undeveloped land in 1905, with the bay shore winding between marsh inlets to the west of the Boulevard. A compass rose stands at the top right beside Baltimore Avenue. The sheet number 59 and 60 references in the right margin point to the adjoining sheets east and south. The rest of sheet 57 carries the title, a key map of Lavallette and Ortley and an inset of the north end of the town, which are separate parts or left out.
notes: Printed sheet number 57 (canvas 1, the title sheet).
The Boulevard is roughly the line of modern Bay Boulevard.
The borough line crosses the bottom of the part below Newark Avenue.

Printed sheet 57 (title page). Scale 120 ft to an inch. Part 1: bay side of Lavallette, Washington Av to Newark Av, between Barnegat Bay, the Boulevard and Baltimore Av. Part 2: inset at bottom right, the lots north of Ortley Av either side of Grand Central Av (north end of sheet 58). The key map of Lavallette and Ortley at top right is not to scale for georeferencing and is left out of the masks.

canvas-01-2.description: This inset at the lower right of sheet 57 shows the northern end of Lavallette, drawn at 120 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, as a strip of lots on the north side of Ortley Avenue either side of Grand Central Avenue. It lies just above the top edge of sheet 58, whose first row of blocks it repeats in outline below Ortley Avenue. West of Grand Central Avenue are lots 1 to 8 of a block marked 5 1/2; east of it lots 1 to 16 of a block marked 1/2, running toward the ocean. One small group of dwellings stands at the ocean end of the eastern lots. Otherwise the strip is empty in 1905. A north arrow and the 120 feet to an inch scale bar are drawn in the inset.
notes: Printed on sheet 57; the area lies north of sheet 58.
Placed from the Ortley Avenue / Grand Central Avenue junction and block corners carried from sheet 58; low confidence.

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 covers the northern half of Lavallette, drawn at 120 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from Ortley Avenue at the top to Philadelphia Avenue at the bottom, and from the shore of Barnegat Bay on the west to Ocean Avenue and the Atlantic beach on the east. Twelve parallel avenues cross the sheet from bay to ocean: Ortley, White, Kerr, Bond, Guyer, President, Reese, Vance, Magee, Brown, Camden and Philadelphia. The single track of the Philadelphia and Long Branch Railroad runs down the sheet between the bay blocks and Grand Central Avenue, and a curving Boulevard follows the bay shore on the west. The blocks are laid out in numbered lots in Sections A and B of the resort plan, and most are still empty in 1905. Buildings are few and scattered: dwellings near the bay and along Grand Central and Ocean Avenues, boat houses and a boat storage shed on the bay at Reese and Guyer Avenues, the Leslie Hotel on the corner of Grand Central and President Avenues, a club house at Magee Avenue, a chapel near Philadelphia Avenue, a group of dwellings and sheds near the Ocean Avenue end of the bottom block, and a frame building marked as being built near White Avenue. Several creeks and inlets of the bay cut into the western blocks, and a narrow channel is cut in from the bay near Reese Avenue. A long yellow dashed line, drawn like a frame structure, runs along the west side of Ocean Avenue for most of the sheet. The sheet carries no water works or fire protection, as the title page notes for the whole town.
notes: The railroad (Philadelphia & Long Branch R.R.) right-of-way is now Anna O Hankins Boulevard.
The Boulevard along the bay is roughly the line of modern Bay Boulevard.
Ocean Avenue is not a street today; the Lavallette boardwalk runs near its line.
Lavallette north: Ortley Av to Philadelphia Av, bay to Ocean Av; Philadelphia & Long Branch R.R. (now Anna O Hankins Boulevard), Grand Central Av. Scale 120 ft to an inch. One part.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 covers the southern half of Lavallette, drawn at 120 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from Philadelphia Avenue at the top to Newark Avenue at the bottom, and from Baltimore Avenue on the west to Ocean Avenue and the Atlantic beach on the east. The cross avenues are Philadelphia, Washington, Brooklyn, New Brunswick, Virginia, Pennsylvania, New York, New Jersey, Jersey City, Princeton, Elizabeth and Newark. The Philadelphia and Long Branch Railroad runs down the sheet between Baltimore and Grand Central Avenues; beside it, between Philadelphia and Brooklyn Avenues, two whole blocks are marked as depot grounds, and a block at the top left is marked as a hotel site. West of Baltimore Avenue the sheet draws only the outlines of the blocks, which are shown in full on sheet 57. Nearly every block is divided into numbered lots of Sections C and D of the resort plan and stands empty in 1905. The only buildings are a handful of dwellings along Ocean Avenue between Philadelphia and Brooklyn Avenues, a group of dwellings at the north end of the ocean block below Philadelphia Avenue, one dwelling at Grand Central and Virginia Avenues, one near the railroad at New York Avenue, and one at the Ocean Avenue end of New Brunswick Avenue. A compass rose and the scale bar stand on the beach between Ocean Avenue and the surf line. The sheet is a planned grid laid out ahead of building, with streets drawn 70 feet wide and Baltimore and Ocean Avenues 100 feet.
notes: The railroad right-of-way is now Anna O Hankins Boulevard.
Ocean Avenue is not a street today; the Lavallette boardwalk runs near its line.
Marked Depot Grounds and Hotel Site blocks at the north end.
Lavallette south: Philadelphia Av to Newark Av, Baltimore Av to Ocean Av; R.R. (now Anna O Hankins Boulevard), Grand Central Av, depot grounds. Scale 120 ft to an inch. One part.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 covers Ortley, south of Lavallette, drawn at 120 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from Newark Avenue at the top, across Trenton Avenue and the dash-dot borough line between Lavallette and Ortley, through 1st to 7th Avenues to the bottom edge, and from Barnegat Avenue on the west to Ocean Avenue and the beach on the east. Between Baltimore and Grand Central Avenues the Philadelphia and Long Branch Railroad runs down the sheet, flanked between 3rd and 5th Avenues by Railway Avenue West and Railway Avenue East, with the small Ortley railroad station and a platform beside the track at 4th Avenue. Two ponds lie in the blocks either side of the railroad between 2nd and 4th Avenues. The blocks are divided into lots numbered up to the 500s, and nearly all are empty in 1905. The buildings stand mainly on the ocean block between 1st and 4th Avenues: the Ortley Inn at Ocean Avenue near 4th Avenue, heated by hot air, with a laundry and servants' quarters, a bath house and a water tank; an Episcopal church near 3rd Avenue; and several dwellings, joined by long yellow dashed lines drawn like frame structures. A post office and a few dwellings stand near Baltimore Avenue, and at the left edge buildings of a farm are partly drawn beyond Barnegat Avenue. The top row of blocks, between Newark and Trenton Avenues, repeats the bottom of sheet 59 and of sheet 57. A compass rose sits in the station block.
notes: Ortley is now Ortley Beach, in Toms River Township.
Barnegat Avenue is now Washington Avenue (Ortley Beach).
The modern 5th, 6th and 7th Avenues do not lie on the 1905 lines; the area south of 4th Avenue was replatted with intermediate streets and is placed by extrapolation.
Modern Ocean Avenue in Ortley Beach lies about 70 m west of the 1905 Ocean Avenue.
The railroad right-of-way is now East Central Avenue.

Ortley (now Ortley Beach, Toms River Township): Newark Av to below 7th Av, Barnegat Av (now Washington Avenue) to Ocean Av; Ortley R.R. station, Ortley Inn, Lavallette-Ortley borough line. Scale 120 ft to an inch. One part.
